# PR #2597: Patch: the AI prices a Starship Piece's death by the copy it fuses into its owner's Starship

Closes #2566

## What changed

When a Starship Piece dies, the death pass fuses a copy of it into its owner's Dormant Starship (R1852000). The AI's Death pricing (R2424000) never counted that, because it only probed units with a live Death hook, and the fusion is a step of the death pass, not a hook. So the AI treated killing an enemy piece as clean removal and valued its own pieces at their stats alone.

- **`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`**
  - A new `leaves_behind` is true for a unit with a live Death (`death_hook_of`) or a unit that is a Starship Piece (`is_starship_piece`, the same reader the death pass's `dies_as_piece` uses: the keyword through the layers, face-up). `death_price` now uses it as its guard.
  - `death_prices` collects candidates in two passes: every live Death first, in R2424000's order, then each piece that has no Death of its own, in the same order. Both share `AI_DEATH_PROBE_NODES`.
  - Probing and keying are unchanged (`death_probe`, `spawned_death_probe`, `DeathPrice::key`/`is_for`, `kill_worth`). The sandbox destroy already runs the death pass, so a probed piece's price includes its fusion.
- **`crates/ai/tests/ai/deaths.rs`**: four `r2566000_*` tests:
  - **Own piece priced:** After Burner (stinkyscape-090) on the AI's board has no Death and is priced at `slumber_waiting_share` × its body (6.4 against 12.8). `unit_worth` adds `AI_EVAL.death` of that price.

# #2566: Patch: the AI prices a Starship Piece's death by the copy it fuses into its owner's Starship
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
In Stinkyscape, a Starship Piece that dies is not simply gone: a copy of it joins its owner's starship, which grows with each piece. The computer opponent prices that death as if nothing were left behind. So it kills an enemy piece as if that were clean removal, when it is actually feeding the enemy ship, and it spends its own pieces as if they were worth no more than their stats. After this change, the AI counts what a piece's death adds to the starship, the same way it already counts what other cards leave behind when they die.

## Why
- R2424000 prices a Unit's death by what it leaves behind, but only through a script's own Death hook. The probe takes candidates with `death_hook_of(world, card).is_some()` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:1195`), and the price is used only `if death_hook_of(state, unit).is_some()` (`evaluate.rs:227`).
- A piece's fusion is not a Death hook. It runs in the engine's death pass: `starship_step` calls `crate::starship::fuse_dead_piece` (`crates/engine/src/state_check.rs:693-699`, R1852000). Cannon v3's header (`crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape/c052_cannon_v3.rs:7`) says "played alone, its death fuses a copy into its owner's Dormant Starship (R1852000)".
- The Death probe already kills the unit through the engine's own sandbox destroy (`SandboxOp::Destroy`, `evaluate.rs:1092`), so a piece let into the probe should show the fusion. The first test proves whether it does.
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/starship.rs:6` still says "No shipped card is a Starship Piece (Stinkyscape's come with the set)". That has been stale since Stinkyscape shipped.
- The learned weights (`crates/ai/src/learned/weights.json`, catalog v0.3.17) hold no Stinkyscape key, so the hand evaluation is the whole price of these cards.

## Proposal
- In the probe's candidate filter and in `death_price`, accept a Unit that is a Starship Piece, read through the layers as the engine reads it, as well as one with a Death hook.
- Fix the stale header of `tests/ai/starship.rs`.
- A new ruling in the issue's block amends what R2424000 prices.

## Where it lands
`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/starship.rs` (or `deaths.rs`), `crates/ai/README.md`, and `spec/rulings/R<n>.md` with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md` (§9.9).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A shipped piece with no Death of its own prices above zero for its owner, at the evaluation change its fusion makes.
- [ ] Given one removal, an enemy piece and an enemy vanilla Unit of equal stats, the AI removes the vanilla Unit.
- [ ] Units with a Death hook price as before, and R2424000's tests are unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` passes at smoke size, and the perf gate holds.

## Size and risks
Small code change, but hard by CLAUDE.md rule 11 (AI). Pieces share `AI_DEATH_PROBE_NODES` with other deaths, so a board full of pieces can crowd out other probes; the test should cover the budget order. Rebase on the open PR #2551 if it lands first, since it also changes how the AI counts its backrow.
